news.casting_brief: Ancient DNA researchers like Ruairidh Macleod, Oxford colleagues, alongside the long-dead hunter-gatherers of Lake Baikal whose teeth still whisper the oldest plague.
news.script_brief: 5,500 years ago, plague sweeps southeastern Siberian hunter-gatherer bands, felling dozens before any farming town exists. Researchers sequence the oldest Yersinia pestis strain from victims' teeth at four cemeteries—rewriting plague's birth. Tension: a 'weak' early strain still killed; the scourge predates rats and settled towns.
news.news_close_brief: The teeth of the dead carry a warning across five and a half millennia: the plague walked among us long before our cities. Its oldest strain is sequenced; its origin story, rewritten.

dramatic_state.dramatic_question: Will the world be told plague predates rats and farming towns before Rei can prove the weak Siberian strain truly killed those hunter-gatherers?
dramatic_state.character_a_wants: To broadcast NOW that the Lake Baikal teeth rewrite plague's birth before rats or towns
dramatic_state.character_b_wants: To prove the 'weak' early Yersinia pestis killed before any claim airs
dramatic_state.ending_change: They air it together: the oldest Yersinia pestis sequence confirms a weak strain still felled Baikal bands 5,500 years ago.

rendered_lines: Tonight on Signal Lost, we journey to the ancient Siberian frost, where the silent graves of wandering hunters hold the terrifying, timeless genesis of Yersinia pestis.

Station Alpha transmitting on all open emergency frequencies. I am declaring a level four breach. The Siberian permafrost containment grid has suffered a catastrophic failure. The Yersinia pestis strain that slaughtered those hunter-gatherers near Lake Baikal... it survived the ice. And now it's out.

I have the telemetry. Inner seals failed three minutes ago. It just chewed through the secondary containment filters. Vector projections are tracking a southern spread at a rate I have never seen modeled. If it reaches the transit corridor, the first populated sectors fall by morning.

I'm dropping the physical blast doors and killing the cold-chain feeds, but that won't hold the Lake Baikal strain if it's already past secondary. Rei, get on that primary console and prep the global emergency broadcast right now. The satellite uplinks are starting to freeze out, and once this local grid completely collapses, we won't be able to push a warning through to anyone.

I'm patching the transmission through the last orbital relay. But Donna... if this strain slaughtered isolated hunter-gatherers long before the first farming town, what chance do our hyper-connected cities have? We aren't sending a warning. We're just broadcasting an obituary.
